clinicalPearls: Recurrent episodes of severe nausea and vomiting in the context of long-term, regular cannabis use
A highly characteristic feature is temporary symptom relief from hot showers or baths
The clinical pattern resembles cyclic vomiting syndrome, with well periods between attacks
It is frequently misdiagnosed, and patients often undergo repeated investigations before it is recognised
Definitive resolution follows sustained cessation of cannabis, which is both diagnostic and therapeutic
Acute episodes are managed supportively, and topical capsaicin and certain antiemetic or sedative agents are used adjunctively
reference.pathophysiology: Cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome is a paradoxical effect of chronic cannabis use, in which prolonged stimulation of the endocannabinoid system disrupts its normal regulation of gastrointestinal motility, the emetic reflex and thermoregulation. Proposed mechanisms include downregulation or dysregulation of cannabinoid receptors and effects on hypothalamic thermoregulatory centres, which may explain the relief obtained from hot water. The syndrome resolves when the causative cannabinoid exposure is removed, confirming its central role.
additionalDifferentials: Raised intracranial pressure or other central cause of vomiting
Metabolic or endocrine causes of recurrent vomiting
additionalInvestigations: History of chronic cannabis use and the hot-water bathing behaviour
Targeted tests to exclude obstruction and metabolic causes rather than repeated broad workup
Assessment of hydration and electrolytes during acute episodes
Consideration of cyclic vomiting syndrome in the differential
Confirmation by resolution with cannabis cessation
redFlags: Neurological signs suggesting a central cause
reference.prognosis: The syndrome resolves fully with sustained cannabis cessation, but recurs if use resumes; complications relate mainly to dehydration and electrolyte disturbance during severe attacks.
pitfalls: Not asking about cannabis use and the hot-water pattern
Repeated extensive investigation before recognising the syndrome
Attributing episodes to cyclic vomiting syndrome without exploring cannabis use
Overlooking dehydration and electrolyte disturbance in acute attacks
references: Sleisenger and Fordtran's Gastrointestinal and Liver Disease
